how_it_wins:
Two engines, and only one of them needs your commander. That is the whole plan, and it is why the first six turns are never a waiting room. The median game casts Gishath, Sun's Avatar on turn eight, so a deck that only starts when he lands starts too late. Build both, and let the table relax at an eight-drop for as long as it likes.

Engine one is the swing. Connect, and every Dinosaur in the reveal walks onto the battlefield for free -- stack 001 turns one seven-damage hit into five new bodies, three cards and a discover at X=6. Take that discover off your biggest toughness before any token enters. Get the order right and the swing pays twice.

Engine two never attacks. With Forerunner of the Empire out, any Dinosaur entering lets you ping the whole board for 1, and stack 005 cashes that single point five ways: a dead token, an opposing 3/3 exiled under Trapjaw Tyrant, a card off Ripjaw Raptor, a tapped Forest off Ranging Raptors, and a fresh 5/5 off Polyraptor. Take the ping every turn you can. The damage wipes off at cleanup; the yield does not.

Now the one thing that beats you, named out loud: you deploy in a single wave, so a sweeper aimed at your swing turn takes all of it. Swing holding Heroic Intervention, Flawless Maneuver, Boros Charm or Akroma's Will -- you will have one by turn six in roughly half your games (48.5%), so steer toward the turn you do. If somebody wipes you anyway, rebuild the Human first: the web comes back on two cards, the commander comes back at eight plus tax.

And you own a wipe that only hurts them. Blasphemous Act under Temple Altisaur deals your other Dinosaurs exactly 1 apiece and 13 to everything else, and stack 004 sends 16 upstairs at a player on the way through. Cast it from behind. You come out further ahead than you went in.

combo_lines.001:
Exhibit one, CR 603.2h: a once-per-turn rider "triggers only if its source's controller has not yet taken the indicated action that turn." Pantlaza, Sun-Favored polices the trigger itself, not merely the payoff.

That cuts both ways in a single event. Four Dinosaurs enter simultaneously with the action untaken, so all four instances trigger and CR 603.3b hands you the ordering. The 3/3 token from Regisaur Alpha enters afterward, once the discover is spent, and never triggers at all.

The holding: you get one discover a turn and you choose which. Biggest toughness on top, token trigger on the bottom -- that ordering is the difference between discover 6 and discover 4.
combo_lines.002:
Read both texts and note what is missing. Marauding Raptor "deals 2 damage to it"; Polyraptor's enrage "create a token." Neither says may, and CR 104.4b is emphatic that "loops that contain an optional action don't result in a draw" -- so the absence of that one word is the entire case.

Two damage never kills a fresh 5/5, each copy is pinged exactly once, and this list fields no sacrifice outlet. CR 732.4: "If a loop contains only mandatory actions, the game is a draw."

The holding: this pairing is not a win condition, it is a motion to end everybody's game. Your opponents hold the only exit, and they will take it at a token count that suits them.
combo_lines.003:
CR 603.5, four words that break an infinite: "The choice is made when the ability resolves." Every sweep Forerunner of the Empire offers is a may, answered fresh each time, which means this chain has a brake fitted as standard.

It also has a fuse. Forerunner takes 1 from its own third sweep and dies at 3, and CR 113.6 confirms that a permanent's abilities function only while it is on the battlefield -- the chain ends because its engine ends.

The holding: seven tokens is the ceiling, and reaching seven takes declining one intermediate trigger rather than saying yes to everything. Bounded above, self-terminating, stoppable at every link. The database calls it infinite; the clause disagrees.
combo_lines.004:
The finest two words on Temple Altisaur are "another Dinosaur." CR 615.1 has prevention shields applying "continuously as events happen," so as Blasphemous Act deals its 13, each of your other Dinosaurs is shielded down to 1 -- and the Altisaur, which is not another Dinosaur to itself, eats the full 13 and dies.

Then the departed testifies. CR 113.7a: when a source has left, "its last known information is used. The source can still perform the action even though it no longer exists." A Dinosaur dealt 13 is a Wrathful Raptors redirect worth 13.

The holding: state-based actions clear the board before targets are chosen (CR 704.3), so by the time the redirects are stacked the only legal non-Dinosaur targets left are players. Thirteen from the dead, one each from three survivors, sixteen at one seat.
combo_lines.005:
The whole case is running order. CR 704.3: the game performs state-based actions and re-checks them, and "otherwise all triggered abilities that are waiting to be put on the stack are put on the stack" -- triggers wait until the dust settles.

So the opposing 1/1 is destroyed by that check before anything is stacked, and CR 115.1d chooses Trapjaw Tyrant's target as its trigger goes on the stack, by which point the 3/3 is the only creature left to take. One optional point of damage produces four enrage triggers, all of them yours to order.

The holding: the Polyraptor copy re-arms Forerunner of the Empire with a genuinely new may, and CR 603.5 lets you answer it no. Declining banks the whole yield and stops the self-damage there.

card_roles.Gishath, Sun's Avatar: Do not swing him for value -- swing him with a lane cleared or a shield in hand, because the connect is the deck and stack 001 prices one hit at five bodies, three cards and a discover. Every death adds two to an eight-mana bill, so make the first swing count.
card_roles.Akroma's Will: With your commander on the battlefield you take both modes: indestructible protection and lethal evasion off one card. It is also one of the few shields wide enough to cover Forerunner of the Empire, which no tribal effect in this list will protect.
card_roles.Alpine Meadow: Tapped R/W snow dual. Drop it on a turn you were not going to spend all your mana anyway.
card_roles.Arcane Signet: Any colour you need, on turn two. Your land drops thin out fast, and rocks are what keep the curve climbing after they do.
card_roles.Austere Command: The sweeper where you pick the survivors -- artifacts plus small creatures usually clears the table and leaves your fat alone. Choose greedily and you will bin your own Signets and dorks with everything else.
card_roles.Beast Within: Instant-speed answer to literally any permanent. Handing back a 3/3 costs you nothing at a table where your average body is twice that.
card_roles.Belbe's Portal: Name Dinosaur, then flash one in from hand for {3} and a tap -- ambush blockers, dodge sorcery-speed removal. Fund it with real mana: neither Unclaimed Territory nor Secluded Courtyard can pay for this activation.
card_roles.Blasphemous Act: Your catch-up button, and with Temple Altisaur out it is a sweeper you are on the right side of. Stack 004 verifies the full package throwing 16 at a player -- and budget for the Altisaur itself, which eats its own 13.
card_roles.Bonehoard Dracosaur: Two free cards to play and a token every upkeep, on a flying first-striker that defends while it pays. It exiles your top two, so cash any stacked top before the upkeep arrives.
card_roles.Boros Charm: Two mana, three answers: indestructible through a wrath, four at a face, or double strike on your biggest attacker. Treat the indestructible mode as worth your whole board, because on the swing turn it is.
card_roles.Boros Signet: Turns colourless mana into the two pips this deck struggles for. Cheap, unglamorous, and exactly what the white and red halves of the curve want.
card_roles.Bronzebeak Foragers: One body, one hostage from every opponent -- and Gishath can put it onto the battlefield for free. They are hostages, not corpses: pay the {X}{W} to bury a card outright before anything can bounce the Foragers.
card_roles.Canopy Vista: G/W, and untapped whenever two basics are already down. With fourteen basics in the list, that is most games.
card_roles.Carnage Tyrant: Uncounterable, untargetable, seven trample power -- the payoff a control seat simply cannot interact with. It is also the best name to see in a reveal, since its toughness sets a discover at X=6.
card_roles.Cinder Glade: R/G once two basics are under you. Lead on basics early and it plays as a real dual all game.
card_roles.City of Brass: Any colour for a point of life. Pay it cheerfully; a missed pip costs far more than the point ever will.
card_roles.Clifftop Retreat: R/W, untapped if you already control a Mountain or a Plains. Eight Mountain-typed and seven Plains-typed lands make that check easy.
card_roles.Command Tower: The best land in the format, doing exactly what it always does. Play it, forget it, thank it later.
card_roles.Congregation at Dawn: Stack the three creatures you want at instant speed, then connect and take all three for free. Cast it when the swing is imminent, not aspirational -- any shuffle undoes the work.
card_roles.Cultivate: A land down and a land in hand: ramp now, plus the drop you will otherwise miss around turn six. Never a bad turn-three play.
card_roles.Curious Altisaur: Every Dinosaur that connects turns into a card, and reach keeps fliers honest while it happens. Attack wide and read the payoff.
card_roles.Descendants' Path: Free casts off the top every upkeep for anything sharing a type with your board, which in a list this dense is often. A miss bottoms the card, so do not stack a tutor target the turn before your upkeep.
card_roles.Eerie Interlude: Blink the team out of a wrath and collect every enters trigger again on the way back. Token copies exiled this way do not return -- count your Polyraptor copies as spent.
card_roles.Enlightened Tutor: One mana for whichever artifact or enchantment the game is asking for: Urza's Incubator for the discount, Mirari's Wake for the mana, Garruk's Uprising for the cards. Cast it on their end step so you draw it immediately.
card_roles.Etali, Primal Storm: Every attack exiles the top card of each library and casts the good ones free -- an engine that scales with the strongest deck at the table, not yours. Give it haste from Otepec Huntmaster or Regisaur Alpha and it pays the turn it lands.
card_roles.Exotic Orchard: Any colour an opponent's lands can make, which at a three-colour table is everything. Only a board of pure colourless mana turns it off.
card_roles.Flawless Maneuver: Free with your commander out, which is precisely the turn you are tapped out and terrified. Indestructible for the team, and it covers Forerunner of the Empire when nothing tribal will.
card_roles.Forbidden Orchard: Perfect fixing that hands an opponent a 1/1 Spirit each time. Aim the Spirits at the seat you are not planning to attack.
card_roles.Forest: Seven copies, and the target every Forest-fetcher in the deck is hunting. Lead on them to switch on the battle lands and check lands.
card_roles.Garruk's Uprising: Trample for the whole team plus a card for every 4-power body that enters -- stack 001 draws exactly three off one reveal. Know the cutoff: 3-power tokens miss, so do not count them.
card_roles.Ghalta and Mavren: Every attack hands you a giant tapped-and-attacking Dinosaur or a lifelinking Vampire army, free, forever. The Dinosaur arrives attacking, so it never blocks for you -- attack anyway.
card_roles.Ghalta, Primal Hunger: Reads twelve mana, costs about three once you have a board, and closes games at 12/12 trample. The discount only applies when you cast it, which matters not at all when a reveal puts it in for nothing.
card_roles.Heroic Intervention: Two mana buys hexproof and indestructible for everything you own. This is the card that justifies leaving one green up on every turn that matters.
card_roles.Huatli, Poet of Unity // Roar of the Fif: A basic to hand on entry, and five mana later she flips into a Saga that makes 3/3s, turns your creatures into mana, tutors a Dinosaur and finishes on team double strike and trample. Flip her the turn before you intend to end somebody.
card_roles.Hulking Raptor: A ramp body with ward {2}, adding {G}{G} at every one of your first mains -- acceleration the removal spell has to pay extra to answer. It pulls the commander forward a full turn on its own.
card_roles.Hunter's Insight: Point it at an unblocked Gishath and draw seven on top of the reveal. Cast it after blockers are declared; you are buying certainty, so buy the certain version.
card_roles.Intrepid Paleontologist: Any-colour mana, graveyard hate, and a way to cast Dinosaurs out of exile, all on a two-drop. Finality counters mean each recovered Dinosaur gets exactly one more life -- spend it on the big one.
card_roles.Itzquinth, Firstborn of Gishath: A hasty two-drop that pays {2} on entry to have your best Dinosaur shoot something -- removal wearing a body. It carries no enrage of its own (verified in stack 005); it starts the web rather than feeding on it.
card_roles.Jetmir's Garden: All three colours tapped, and a card via cycling once the game is long. Early land drop or late cantrip, never a dead draw.
card_roles.Kessig Wolf Run: A colourless land right up until it is the kill: {X}{R}{G} makes any creature bigger and trampling. Every spare Polyraptor token is one activation from unblockable maths.
card_roles.Kodama's Reach: Cultivate's twin, and redundancy in the effect your whole schedule rides is not filler. Land down, land banked.
card_roles.Krosan Verge: Cracks into a Forest and a Plains, and the typed duals count -- two lands from one drop is exactly what a fading land-drop rate wants. It enters tapped, so put it down early and crack it whenever.
card_roles.Mirari's Wake: Team +1/+1 and every land taps twice, which turns your eight-drops into five-drops the turn after it sticks. This is what Enlightened Tutor fetches when the plan is simply to go over everybody.
card_roles.Monster Manual // Zoological Study: The cheap way to put a creature from hand onto the battlefield, with an adventure half that mills five and returns a creature first. Same mana rule as the Portal: neither typal land can pay the activation.
card_roles.Mountain: Four copies of the red anchor, and the check that switches on Cinder Glade, Clifftop Retreat, Rootbound Crag and Commercial District.
card_roles.Myriad Landscape: A land that becomes two basics of a shared type. It is tapped at both ends, so start the process early rather than on the turn you need mana.
card_roles.Nature's Lore: A Forest-typed land onto the battlefield untapped, and twelve of this deck's lands carry the type -- turn two into Canopy Vista is fixing and ramp at once. The untapped clause is the whole card.
card_roles.Otepec Huntmaster: Dinosaurs cost one less and something gets haste every turn for free, which is how a discovered Carnage Tyrant attacks immediately. It is a 1/1 Human, so it dies to your own Blasphemous Act along with everything else.
card_roles.Overwhelming Stampede: +X/+X and trample off your biggest power -- with Gishath or a Ghalta down, that is table-ending arithmetic. Cast it after the reveal fills the board, never before.
card_roles.Pantlaza, Sun-Favored: Free spells off every Dinosaur entering, once a turn, with no combat and no eight mana required -- the engine that still works the turn after a wrath. Sequencing is everything: stack 001 verifies that you take the discover off your largest toughness before any token enters.
card_roles.Path of Ancestry: Any commander colour plus a scry on nearly every creature you cast, since most of the roster shares a type with Gishath. Small edges, every single turn.
card_roles.Path to Exile: One mana, exile anything. The basic they get is a real gift early, so spend this on the card that threatens your plan rather than the one that annoys you.
card_roles.Plains: Three copies of the white anchor, and the target Windswept Heath and Krosan Verge both go looking for.
card_roles.Pugnacious Hammerskull: A big body for three mana that simply attacks. Swing it only with a second Dinosaur out or it stuns itself -- a bar this deck clears easily.
card_roles.Quartzwood Crasher: Trample damage mints an X/X trample Dinosaur equal to the damage dealt, and Garruk's Uprising gives everything trample. Leave it alone two turns and it builds its own army.
card_roles.Regal Imperiosaur: A three-mana lord handing every other Dinosaur +1/+1. It quietly moves half your roster past both combat maths and sweeper maths.
card_roles.Regisaur Alpha: Haste for the team and a 3/3 trampler on arrival -- the name you most want to see in a reveal when the new board needs to matter. Stack 001's fine print: that haste is insurance for the next swing, not a second combat now.
card_roles.Ripjaw Raptor: Damage in, card out, verified drawing live in stacks 004 and 005. Let it get hit -- by blockers, by your own pings, by anybody's spite; that is the business model, not an accident.
card_roles.Rishkar's Expertise: Draw cards equal to your biggest power, then cast something worth five or less for free. Cast it the turn after a reveal, when your board is embarrassing.
card_roles.Rogue's Passage: Four mana makes Gishath unblockable, and the connect is the entire deck. Save the activation for the turn a connect actually converts.
card_roles.Rootbound Crag: R/G, untapped with a Mountain or a Forest down -- a check this deck almost always passes.
card_roles.Secluded Courtyard: Name Dinosaur and it pays for Dinosaur spells and for the abilities of Dinosaur creatures too; the clause is more generous than its reputation. It still cannot fund Belbe's Portal or Monster Manual, which are artifacts rather than creature sources.
card_roles.Skyshroud Claim: Two Forest-typed lands onto the battlefield untapped, duals included -- Canopy Vista plus Cinder Glade fixes everything in one card. The four-mana price is the only cost.
card_roles.Sol Ring: Sol Ring. There is no turn on which you are unhappy to see it.
card_roles.Sunpetal Grove: G/W, untapped with a Forest or Plains already down. This deck passes that check in its sleep.
card_roles.Swords to Plowshares: One mana, the problem is gone, and the life they gain has never blocked anybody. Spend it on commanders and engines, not on bodies you can simply out-size.
card_roles.Talisman of Unity: G/W on turn two, with an optional point of pain. Take the damage when the colour matters and the colourless when it does not.
card_roles.Temple Altisaur: Your enrage governor: every damage source hits your other Dinosaurs for exactly 1, which turns sweepers into triggers. Two traps verified in stack 004 -- it never shields itself, and a Human is not a Dinosaur, so Forerunner of the Empire stays exposed.
card_roles.Thrashing Brontodon: A real body that sacrifices at instant speed to kill any artifact or enchantment. Hold the activation for the piece that actually locks you out, not the first mana rock you see.
card_roles.Topiary Stomper: Ramp stapled to a 4/4: a basic straight onto the battlefield when it enters. It cannot attack or block until you control seven lands, which is fine -- you hired it for the land.
card_roles.Triumphant Chomp: One red mana for damage equal to your biggest Dinosaur's power, which most turns is a one-mana kill spell. It is a sorcery, so the ambush everyone imagines is not on the menu.
card_roles.Trumpeting Carnosaur: Discover 5 when it enters, or pay {2}{R} and discard it for 3 damage to a creature or planeswalker. A six-drop that is never a dead card in any hand is doing two jobs at once.
card_roles.Unclaimed Territory: Any colour, for Dinosaur spells and nothing else. It will never activate Belbe's Portal or Monster Manual, so treat it as cast-plan mana only.
card_roles.Urza's Incubator: Two mana off every Dinosaur in the deck, the commander included -- the biggest single discount available to you, and it drags his arrival forward on its own. Enlightened Tutor's first choice when your hand is full of fat.
card_roles.Vaultborn Tyrant: Three life and a card whenever a 4-power body enters, itself included, and it leaves a copy behind when it dies. This is the card that makes attrition tables regret the plan.
card_roles.Wakening Sun's Avatar: Destroy every non-Dinosaur creature -- a wrath you are on the winning side of. It only fires when cast from your hand, so a reveal or a Portal drop skips the wipe entirely.
card_roles.Wayward Swordtooth: An extra land drop every turn for two mana, in a deck whose drops dry up by midgame. It needs the city's blessing to fight, and you do not care; ten permanents arrives sooner than you think.
card_roles.Worldly Tutor: One green mana puts any creature on top, which with a connect coming reads as putting your best Dinosaur onto the battlefield. The cleanest setup card in the list.
card_roles.Zacama, Primal Calamity: Nine mana that untaps your lands when you cast it, so it is nearly free the turn it resolves, then it burns, kills artifacts and gains life on demand. Cheat it in and you get no untap -- 'if you cast it' means what it says.
card_roles.Selvala, Heart of the Wilds: One green mana taps her for X equal to your greatest power, which any 5/5 turns into a commander years ahead of schedule. Every experienced table kills her on sight, so deploy her the turn you can spend the mana, not the turn before.
card_roles.Regal Behemoth: Monarch on entry and an extra mana of any colour off every land while you hold the crown -- a mana engine on a 5/5 trample body. The crown paints you; welcome the extra card each turn nobody manages to take it.
card_roles.Forerunner of the Empire: The hub of engine two: it stacks a Dinosaur on top when it enters, and every Dinosaur entering afterwards offers a 1-damage sweep that switches enrage on (stacks 003 and 005). Protect the 1/3 Human with your board-wide instants, because Temple Altisaur will not, the typal lands will not, and Gishath's reveal never finds it.
card_roles.Polyraptor: Damage in, another Polyraptor out -- one ping makes a 5/5 (stack 005), and the full Forerunner chain caps at seven tokens before shutting itself off (stack 003). Never share a battlefield with Marauding Raptor without an exit: stack 002 makes that loop mandatory, and mandatory loops draw the game.
card_roles.Wrathful Raptors: Every point your Dinosaurs absorb gets thrown at something that is not one, which under Blasphemous Act is 16 upstairs (stack 004). One honest unknown: whether a Forerunner ping with this out still marks damage on your own Dinosaurs is unresolved rules territory -- do not bank the enrage yield with both on the battlefield.
card_roles.Ranging Raptors: Ramp that runs on damage: each ping fetches a tapped basic, verified live in stack 005. Anyone's damage counts, so let it block, let it get swept, let it soak your own sweeps.
card_roles.Trapjaw Tyrant: Repeatable exile removal, one ping one hostage (stack 005). Track what it is holding -- the moment Trapjaw leaves the battlefield, everything comes home at once.
card_roles.Windswept Heath: One life for any Forest or Plains card, typed duals very much included. Crack it at end of turn unless you need the colour right now.
card_roles.Commercial District: Tapped R/G with a surveil attached -- a free look that can bin a dead top card before an upkeep reveal. Small filter, right colours.
card_roles.Arctic Treeline: Tapped G/W snow dual. Same rule as every tapped land here: it goes down on a cheap turn, never the one before the big cast.

mulligan:
This deck keeps. Treat the mulligan button as a tool for two specific hands, not a general anxiety -- opening sevens survive here better than three times in four (77.1%), and a game costs you under a third of a mulligan (0.28). Everything else in the pile is a hand you should be glad to see.

The standard is simple: two to four lands and one card that does something before turn four. Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Talisman of Unity, Nature's Lore, Cultivate, Kodama's Reach, Skyshroud Claim, Topiary Stomper, Wayward Swordtooth -- any of them starts the schedule. Urza's Incubator and Otepec Huntmaster count too; they attack the same problem from the discount side.

Keep every hand that starts the web. Forerunner of the Empire plus any Dinosaur is a two-card engine that needs no combat and no eight mana, and you saw how many bodies the roster can feed it. That hand is doing real work on turn four while the rest of the table is still setting up.

Ship two hands. The first is the shrine to the top end -- Ghalta, Primal Hunger, Zacama, Primal Calamity, Wakening Sun's Avatar and Vaultborn Tyrant with no ramp underneath them -- because a hand full of the second act is a hand with no first act. The second is the mana extreme: nought or one land, or six-plus with nothing to spend them on.

Two judgement calls, made for you. Four lands is not flood in this deck -- your drops thin out badly by turn six, so early surplus is banked, not wasted. And do not mulligan hunting for protection; keep the hand that builds a board worth shielding and hold Heroic Intervention or Flawless Maneuver when it arrives.

One trap worth naming. A hand of Jetmir's Garden, Path of Ancestry and Krosan Verge looks like three lands and behaves like two, since twelve of the thirty-five enter tapped. Keep it when you have a one- or two-mana play to spend those tapped turns on, and think much harder when your cheapest card costs four.
upgrades:
Ten slots, and here is where they came from. Four of the ten are cards already in the sideboard; the other six are scouted out of the wider pool, each beating the twenty-one-card sideboard on a claim it could not match. Four in twenty-one clearing that bar is a depth reading, not a shortfall -- it says the sideboard is real, and that the next big gain lives outside the box.

Read the evidence tags like a portfolio. Seven of the ten carry a "needs a stack scenario" flag, which is not a weakness so much as a price: the biggest ceilings on this list are unresolved rules interactions, and an unresolved ceiling is a promissory note, not income. The three that carry no flag -- two turn-two ramp spells and a lifegain body -- are the settled arithmetic on the sheet.

The cheapest picks are also the most-played, which is usually the tell that a deck is short something ordinary. Farseek sits at EDHREC rank 23 and Three Visits at 42 against a commander whose mean goldfish cast is turn 7.969; a full turn shaved off the ramp step is a full turn off that number, and neither pick asks the deck to learn a new trick. Repercussion at rank 2975 is the other end of the same list: rare, specific, and aimed squarely at a sweep this deck already casts.

The rest lean on the engine you already draw. The enrage web shows up by turn six in 72.6% of games, so every web-extension pick is riding a machine that is usually there rather than one that has to be assembled. That is a better place to spend a slot than the top end, where 5.486 mean available mana at turn six is the real constraint.

One figure frames all ten: every bracket delta reads 4 to 4. The computed floor rides a single combo-database tag on Polyraptor plus Forerunner of the Empire, and stack 003 bounds that pair at seven tokens -- so this is shopping for power inside a bracket conversation the deck is already having, not a step up out of it. The one gap the numbers cannot fill is card draw, where the role budget reads short and the obsolescence index has nothing to offer that beats what the list already runs.
mana_base:
Thirty-five lands across twenty-four entries, and twelve of them enter tapped -- a 34% tap rate, just over the one-in-three the audit allows itself. Seven of those twelve are tapped unconditionally; the rest are check lands and battle lands that pass their test once basics are down. Call it a third of your mana asking for the turn before it works.

The interesting disagreement is between what the deck spends and what it holds. Green writes 56.2% of the pips and holds only 40.0% of the sources. Red runs the opposite book, 19.8% of the pips on 32.0% of the sources, and white sits nearly square at 24.0% on 28.0%. Green is the colour the deck over-asks for, and 54 green pips across 38 cards is why.

The on-curve rates price that gap and then close most of it. Lands alone, the pips arrive on schedule 58.0% of the time in green, 44.6% in red and 37.3% in white. Fold in five rocks and three dorks and those become 74.2%, 58.0% and 58.0% -- white gains better than twenty points, which means the nonland producers are not garnish, they are half the white mana base.

What the rest of the acceleration buys is a curve that keeps climbing after the lands stop. The land-drop hit rate slides from 89.4% on turn three to 52.6% by turn six and 36.2% by turn ten, while mean available mana still reaches 5.486 at turn six and 7.321 at turn ten. Six land-ramp spells and three cost reducers are doing that work; the deck is designed to outlive its own land drops.

Two notes on how the tables count. The 90% yardstick works out to 36 sources per colour against a richest-colour land count of 20 -- in a 35-land deck that is a ruler, not a reachable figure, and rocks and dorks lift the totals to G26/R20/W20. And the audit scores restricted mana at zero, so both typal lands read as no sources at all, even though Secluded Courtyard's clause reaches Dinosaur creature abilities and Unclaimed Territory's stops at Dinosaur spells.
threat_assessment:
Here's what the table sees when you sit down: an eight-mana commander in the command zone and a player they figure they can ignore for seven turns. They're reading the clock right — Gishath's mean cast turn is 7.969, median 8, on the battlefield by turn 6 in just 8.3% of goldfish games. They're reading the seat completely wrong. That gap is where you win, and your first six turns exist to keep it open.

Start winning before the deck is cut. The pregame conversation is yours to run, so run it like a closer — smile on, receipts out. The bracket report computes a floor of 4. Say so first; never let someone else break your own news.

Then show your work. The entire jump from 3 to 4 rides one driver: the combo database tags Polyraptor plus Forerunner of the Empire as a two-card infinite. Your checker resolved that exact pairing on a real board (stack 003, verdict: pass). The verified ceiling is seven Polyraptor tokens — a number you only reach by DECLINING an intermediate trigger, because saying yes to everything caps at six.

The chain stops itself when Forerunner dies to its own third sweep, and every link is a 'you may.' Bounded, controllable, done. The famously unbounded partner, Marauding Raptor, is not in your 99. And stack 002 (verdict: pass) shows that pairing isn't even a win — it's a mandatory whole-table DRAW under CR 732.4 and 104.4b.

matchups:

Your board arrives as one wrath-sized package; deploying in waves is structurally off the menu, because the Gishath trigger IS the wave. So make every sweeper pay retail. You hold that protection by turn 6 in 48.5% of games. In the games you don't, you're not stalled — you're accruing. The ping web's yield banks permanently: Ranging Raptors' Forests stay on the battlefield, and Ripjaw Raptor's cards stay in your hand, through any wrath ever printed.

Know your exposure honestly. Land-drop hit rate falls to 52.6% by turn 6 and mean available mana is 5.486, so mid-game you're riding rocks and dorks a hard sweep can take with it. Favor the land ramp — Cultivate, Kodama's Reach, Nature's Lore — into a suspected wrath turn.

Spend your six spot-removal slots on the one piece that turns off your cheat layer specifically, not the piece that annoys you most. You field 34 must-answer bodies; a stax engine is load-bearing on maybe three cards. Break one and walk through the door they were paid to hold shut.

VS ENRAGE-HOSTILE BOARDS — the go-wide tables you can't race, and the boards that punish a ping. Against the swarm, you're holding the verified trump card. Your marked damage clears at every cleanup. Their board doesn't come back from an exile. And the board that hates your pings is exactly the board Blasphemous Act loves. Either way, you're holding the better end of the mathematics — play it like you know it.
